rv.q: I went in fearing the worst, in all honesty, but this is a production that, even if it is never going to supplant the film, at least delivers moments of communal intensity.
None of it is half as shocking, entertaining or as poignant as the film.
It's a depressing concoction, with misjudged songs and a plot as obscure as an addict's mumblings.
This misfiring adaptation is the perfect case in point that not every story should be turned into a musical.
I can't tell you what this show wants to be but it definitely doesn't want to be a musical.
Ultimately it's the ineptitude rather than the tricky subject matter that sinks Trainspotting The Musical.

cn.t: Critics largely pan this musical adaptation as misconceived and leaden, failing to capture the original's visceral energy. A few find modest merit, but most question why it exists at all.
